question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,1]\times [1,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=4x{y}^{2}+3{x}^{2}-6xy-x. $$ Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[1,\,2]^{T}.$
$[$ {{field-1}} $10$ $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ $-9$ $]$
$10$ {{field-2}} {{field-3}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

$$
{H}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-∇f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(4x{y}^{2}+3{x}^{2}-6xy-x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(4x{y}^{2}+3{x}^{2}-6xy-x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}+6x-6y-1 \\ 8xy-6x\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(4{y}^{2}+6x-6y-1) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(8xy-6x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(4{y}^{2}+6x-6y-1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(8xy-6x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 8y-6 \\ 8y-6 & 8x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}6 & 8y-6 \\ 8y-6 & 8x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}+6x-6y-1 \\ 8xy-6x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}6 & 8y-6 \\ 8y-6 & 8x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}+6x-6y-1 \\ 8xy-6x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & 8(2)-6 \\ 8(2)-6 & 8(1)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}4(2)^{2}+6(1)-6(2)-1 \\ 8(1)(2)-6(1)\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & 10 \\ 10 & 8\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ -10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
